races.title: State Assembly, District 64
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Blanca Pacheco
cands.bio: Attorney and Democrat who has represented California's 64th Assembly District since December 2022. Earlier she was a Downey city councilmember (elected 2016) and Mayor of Downey (2020). She has practiced law, worked as a real estate broker and taught paralegal courses at Downey Adult School.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Pacheco was born or when her family came to California. We found no statements or actions from her on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, growth and land protection, H-1B or immigration enforcement, abortion, or school choice. Her campaign site says she supports police funding and tougher gun laws, but gives no specifics. The pages we read do not describe any bills or deeds that match those topics. The campaign site's description of her priorities was cut off partway through the housing section. Her 2022, 2024 and 2026 Ballotpedia survey responses are blank, so there is no questionnaire to draw on.

local.label: Roots 90: Her campaign biography says she attended elementary school in Cudahy and middle and high school in Downey, and she has held office in Downey and the Assembly; no birthplace appears in the pages I read.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Assembly member since December 2022; Downey City Council from 2016 and Mayor of Downey from 2020; practicing attorney (estates, probate, municipal law) and former real estate broker; former president of the League of California Cities Los Angeles Division.
qual.why: She has prior legislative service in the Assembly, plus local elected office and a law career. Her Rules Committee chair role and civic board roles were not counted.
qual.label: She has prior legislative service in the Assembly, plus local elected office and a law career. Her Rules Committee chair role and civic board roles were not counted.

second-amendment.evidence: Her campaign site says she wants to "enact tougher laws to combat gun violence," alongside prioritizing public safety funding.

cands.name: Raul Ortiz Jr.
cands.bio: Ordained minister and Republican candidate from La Mirada. He has worked in the pest management industry and describes himself as a business leader. Served as second vice president of the California Republican Assembly Fullerton Chapter. He has never held elected office and ran for Assembly District 64 in 2022, 2024 and 2026.

endorsements.text: California Republican Assembly and GOP Union Caucus, as listed on his campaign website.
Republican Party of California (2024). For 2026, Ballotpedia lists Reform California and several voter-guide recommendations, including The Morning Answer with Jennifer Horn.

cands.gaps: He has never held elected office, so there are no votes, bills or official actions to report. We found no statements from him on data centers, development or growth limits, homestead property tax elimination, limits on investor or foreign land buying, or H-1B and immigration enforcement beyond a general campaign-site line about protecting borders. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2024 or 2026 candidate surveys, so his only detailed Q&A is from 2022. His stated positions come from his own campaign materials, and we found no news coverage of him. We could not verify whether he owns a business, or its size, beyond his own description. We did not find the year he started in pest management.

local.label: Roots 100: His campaign site says he was born in Downey, raised in Norwalk and now lives in La Mirada, and Ballotpedia also lists Downey, CA as his birthplace.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Ordained minister for about 41 years, with a career in the pest management industry and a self-described business leader role. He has held no elected office. He has been second vice president of a California Republican Assembly chapter board, which is a party-affiliated volunteer board.
qual.why: He has no legislative, policy or budget work on record. The middle band applies because of his business and management background, but ownership and size of any business are not independently documented, so the score sits at the low end of that band.
qual.label: He has no legislative, policy or budget work on record. The middle band applies because of his business and management background, but ownership and size of any business are not independently documented, so the score sits at the low end of that band.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: In his 2022 Ballotpedia survey he said he would advocate for the California School Choice voter initiative so all parents can choose their child's education path.

pro-life.evidence: In his 2022 Ballotpedia survey he said he would "protect the life of every unborn and born child."

second-amendment.evidence: In his 2022 Ballotpedia survey he pledged to "honor our 1st and 2nd Amendment Rights." He gave no specific gun policies.

back-police-order.evidence: In his 2022 Ballotpedia survey he said he is pro law enforcement, would work to reverse the effects of Prop 47 and would "REFUND" sheriffs and police departments. His campaign site lists "Supporting Law & Order."

prio.label: Matches 4 of 4 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 4 only promised
